## What this notebook does

Notebook 04 proved the radar method on one 2-hour window. This notebook runs
the same method for **every night of spring migration** at each Southern
California radar station, and produces one row per station per night:
how many birds passed, when traffic peaked, and which way they flew.

## The storage problem, and our solution

A full night at one station is about 70 radar scans, roughly 0.5–1 GB of raw
data. All of spring at three stations is **over 150 GB**. But we only need the *bird profiles* that vol2bird extracts, which are
tiny (kilobytes per night). So for each night we:

1. **download** that night's raw scans into a temporary folder,
2. **process** them into bird profiles,
3. **save** the small results,
4. **delete** the temporary folder, then move to the next night.

At most one night of raw data is ever on disk. We also record how much raw
data each night was, so the report can state the true volume we processed.

**It can resume.** Each finished night is saved as its own file. If the run
stops (laptop sleeps, Wi-Fi drops, RStudio closes), re-running skips every
night already done. You can run the season over several sittings.

## How to run

1. Run **Setup** and **Settings**.
2. **First, a timing test:** keep `TEST_RUN <- TRUE` (one station, one week).
   Check the timing and results, then set it to `FALSE` for the full season.
3. Run **Process the season**. Expect roughly 2–5 minutes per night,
   mostly downloading; a full station-season can take a few hours. Leave
   RStudio open and plugged in; interruptions are fine (see above).
4. Run **Combine** and **Plot** whenever you want an up-to-date picture.
   They only read finished nights.

```{r setup}
source(here::here("R", "config.R"))

library(bioRad)     # NEXRAD download + profile tools (uses vol2birdR inside)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Downloads of large radar files can exceed R's default 60-second timeout.
options(timeout = 600)
```

## Settings

```{r settings}
# --- Which nights ------------------------------------------------------------
# Spring window: matches BirdCast's spring monitoring season (Mar 1 – Jun 15),
# which brackets the spring migration dates of all our songbird species.
# These are LOCAL dates: "2026-04-27" means the night that starts on the
# evening of April 27.
SEASON_START <- as.Date("2026-03-01")
SEASON_END   <- as.Date("2026-06-15")

# --- Which stations ----------------------------------------------------------
# From config.R (KNKX San Diego, KSOX Santa Ana Mtns, KVTX Los Angeles).
# Verify the codes on NOAA's station map before the full run.
STATIONS <- RADAR_STATIONS

# --- Timing test ---------------------------------------------------------------
# TRUE  = one station, one week (to measure speed before committing hours).
# FALSE = every station, every night of the season.
TEST_RUN <- FALSE

if (TEST_RUN) {
  STATIONS     <- STATIONS[1]
  SEASON_START <- as.Date("2026-04-21")
  SEASON_END   <- as.Date("2026-04-27")
}

nights <- seq(SEASON_START, SEASON_END, by = "day")

NIGHT_EVERY <- c(KNKX = 1, KSOX = 1, KVTX = 1)

jobs <- map_dfr(STATIONS, \(s) tibble(
  station = s,
  night   = nights[seq(1, length(nights), by = NIGHT_EVERY[[s]])]
))

message(nrow(jobs), " station-nights planned")

# --- Where results go ------------------------------------------------------------
# Small, permanent results (kept, committed to Git):
RADAR_OUT <- file.path(PATHS$derived, "radar", SEASON_LABEL)
dir.create(file.path(RADAR_OUT, "profiles"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(RADAR_OUT, "nights"),   recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Big, temporary raw scans (deleted after each night; data/raw is git-ignored):
RADAR_TMP <- file.path(PATHS$radar, "tmp")

message(length(STATIONS), " station(s) x ", length(nights), " nights = ",
        length(STATIONS) * length(nights), " station-nights")
```

## The one-night function

Everything for one station-night happens inside `process_night()`.

```{r process-night}
#' Download, process, save and clean up ONE station-night.
#'
#' @param station NEXRAD code, e.g. "KNKX".
#' @param night   Local date the night STARTS on (evening of this date).
#' @return Invisibly, the one-row nightly summary (also saved to disk).
process_night <- function(station, night) {

  tag        <- paste0(station, "_", format(night, "%Y-%m-%d"))
  night_file <- file.path(RADAR_OUT, "nights",   paste0(tag, ".csv"))
  prof_file  <- file.path(RADAR_OUT, "profiles", paste0(tag, ".rds"))

  # --- Resume: skip nights already finished -----------------------------------
  if (file.exists(night_file)) {
    message(tag, ": already done, skipping")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # --- Time window ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Radar files are stamped in UTC. Pacific time is UTC-7 (PDT) or UTC-8 (PST),
  # so a local night (sunset to sunrise) falls between about 00:00 and
  # 15:00 UTC on the NEXT calendar day. We download that whole window and let
  # check_night() (below) keep only the scans between sunset and sunrise.
  utc_day  <- night + 1
  date_min <- as.POSIXct(paste(utc_day, "00:00"), tz = "UTC")
  date_max <- as.POSIXct(paste(utc_day, "15:00"), tz = "UTC")

  # --- Temporary folder for this night's raw scans ----------------------------
  # One folder per station-night. on.exit() deletes it when this function
  # finishes, whether it succeeded OR failed, so raw data never piles up.
  # It only ever deletes this one temporary folder.
  tmp <- file.path(RADAR_TMP, tag)
  dir.create(tmp, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  on.exit(unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)

  t0 <- Sys.time()

  # Helper: save a summary row that says why a night has no data, so the
  # resume logic doesn't retry known-empty nights forever.
  save_status <- function(status, n_files = 0, raw_mb = 0) {
    row <- tibble(station, night, status, n_scans = 0L, n_files, raw_mb,
                  total_passage = NA_real_, peak_mtr = NA_real_,
                  peak_time_local = NA_character_, mean_mtr = NA_real_,
                  mean_vid = NA_real_, mean_ff = NA_real_, mean_dd = NA_real_,
                  minutes = round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins")), 2))
    write_csv(row, night_file)
    invisible(row)
  }

  # --- 1. Download ------------------------------------------------------------
  # NOAA's public archive on AWS. A station can be offline for maintenance,
  # so "no files" is recorded as a status rather than treated as a crash.
  dl <- tryCatch(
    download_pvolfiles(date_min, date_max, radar = station, directory = tmp),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  files <- list.files(tmp, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  files <- files[!grepl("_MDM$", files)]   # skip small metadata files
  raw_mb <- round(sum(file.size(files)) / 1e6)

  if (length(files) == 0) {
    message(tag, ": no radar files (station offline?)")
    return(save_status("no data"))
  }

  # --- 2. Process -------------------------------------------------------------
  # Same settings as notebook 04 (see its comments for why).
  vp_list <- lapply(files, \(f) tryCatch(
    calculate_vp(f, rcs = RADAR_RCS, h_layer = 200, n_layer = 20, dual_pol = TRUE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  ))
  vp_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), vp_list)

  if (length(vp_list) < 2) {
    message(tag, ": too few readable scans")
    return(save_status("unreadable", length(files), raw_mb))
  }

  vpts <- bind_into_vpts(vp_list)

  # --- 3. Save ----------------------------------------------------------------
  # (a) The full altitude profiles, so we can revisit flight heights later
  #     without re-downloading anything. Small (tens of KB per night).
  saveRDS(vpts, prof_file)

  # (b) Collapse altitudes and keep only scans between sunset and sunrise.
  #     Daytime echoes are mostly insects.
  vpi <- integrate_profile(vpts)
  scans <- as.data.frame(vpi) |>
    mutate(is_night = check_night(vpi)) |>
    filter(is_night) |>
    arrange(datetime)

  if (nrow(scans) < 2) {
    return(save_status("no night scans", length(files), raw_mb))
  }

  # (c) One summary row for the night.
  #
  # total_passage: birds crossing a 1 km line during the whole night. MTR is a
  # RATE (birds per km per hour), so we multiply each scan's rate by the time
  # until the next scan and add them up. Gaps longer than 1 hour (outages) are
  # capped at 1 hour so a missing stretch doesn't inflate the total.
  #
  # mean_dd: average flight direction. Directions are circular (359° and 1°
  # are neighbours), so we average them as compass vectors, weighted by MTR so
  # busy scans count more than nearly empty ones.
  hours_to_next <- as.numeric(difftime(lead(scans$datetime), scans$datetime, units = "hours"))
  hours_to_next <- pmin(coalesce(hours_to_next, median(hours_to_next, na.rm = TRUE)), 1)

  w <- coalesce(scans$mtr, 0)
  rad <- scans$dd * pi / 180
  ok <- !is.na(rad)
  mean_dd <- (atan2(sum(w[ok] * sin(rad[ok])), sum(w[ok] * cos(rad[ok]))) * 180 / pi) %% 360

  peak <- which.max(scans$mtr)

  row <- tibble(
    station, night, status = "ok",
    n_scans         = nrow(scans),
    n_files         = length(files),
    raw_mb,
    total_passage   = round(sum(scans$mtr * hours_to_next, na.rm = TRUE)),
    peak_mtr        = round(scans$mtr[peak]),
    peak_time_local = format(with_tz(scans$datetime[peak], "America/Los_Angeles"), "%H:%M"),
    mean_mtr        = round(mean(scans$mtr, na.rm = TRUE)),
    mean_vid        = round(mean(scans$vid, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    mean_ff         = round(mean(scans$ff,  na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean_dd         = round(mean_dd) %% 360,   # so 359.7° shows as 0, not 360
    minutes         = round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins")), 2)
  )
  write_csv(row, night_file)

  # --- 4. Delete --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Happens automatically via on.exit() above, as this function returns.
  message(sprintf("%s: %d scans, %d MB raw, %.1f min, passage %s birds/km",
                  tag, row$n_scans, raw_mb, row$minutes,
                  format(row$total_passage, big.mark = ",")))
  invisible(row)
}
```

## Process the season

```{r run}
# Every station x every night. If one night errors unexpectedly, we log it
# and keep going; a failed night has no result file, so a re-run retries it.
jobs <- expand_grid(station = STATIONS, night = nights)

t_start <- Sys.time()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(jobs))) {
  tryCatch(
    process_night(jobs$station[i], jobs$night[i]),
    error = function(e) message(jobs$station[i], " ", jobs$night[i],
                                ": FAILED (", conditionMessage(e), "), will retry next run")
  )
}
message("Session finished in ",
        round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t_start, units = "mins")), 1), " min")
```

## Combine

```{r combine}
# Gather every finished night into one table.
nightly <- list.files(file.path(RADAR_OUT, "nights"), pattern = "\\.csv$",
                      full.names = TRUE) |>
  map_dfr(\(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE,
                        col_types = cols(night = col_date(),
                                         peak_time_local = col_character())))

write_csv(nightly, file.path(PATHS$derived,
                             paste0("radar_", SEASON_LABEL, "_nightly.csv")))

# Progress and "big data" bookkeeping for the report's methods section.
nightly |>
  group_by(station) |>
  summarise(
    nights_done     = n(),
    nights_ok       = sum(status == "ok"),
    scans_processed = sum(n_scans),
    raw_gb          = round(sum(raw_mb) / 1000, 1),
    hours_spent     = round(sum(minutes) / 60, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Plot

```{r plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
p <- nightly |>
  filter(status == "ok") |>
  ggplot(aes(night, total_passage)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1f6fb2", width = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ station, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %d") +
  labs(
    title = paste("Nightly", SEASON_LABEL, "migration over Southern California"),
    subtitle = "Birds crossing a 1 km line per night (vol2bird, 11 cm² per bird)",
    x = NULL, y = "Birds per km per night",
    caption = "Data: NOAA NEXRAD Level II via AWS; processed with vol2bird / bioRad (Dokter et al. 2011)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

p
ggsave(file.path(PATHS$figures, paste0("05_radar_", SEASON_LABEL, "_nightly.png")),
       p, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 200)
```

## Checks before trusting the season

- **Direction:** most `ok` nights should have `mean_dd` roughly northward
  (about 300–45°). Nights pointing south are worth a look: often rain the
  filter missed, or insects.
- **Gaps:** `no data` nights are station outages; note them in the report
  rather than treating them as zero migration.
- **Magnitude:** spot-check 3–4 busy nights against the BirdCast dashboard
  for the same county and date.
- **Timing:** the busiest weeks should overlap the peak weeks from notebook 02.
  That overlap (or a mismatch) is one of the main results to discuss.
